\subsubsection{Bipolar Accuracy}\label{sss:pixel-accuracy}

Figure~\ref{fig:px-xover-ierr} sweeps the truth current $i_{\mathrm{we}}$
through zero at the operational $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ tap. The error
crosses zero smoothly, with no kink between the sourcing and sinking halves of
the sweep: the same TIA feedback path carries current in both directions, so
there is no crossover distortion of the kind a complementary NMOS/PMOS mirror
front end would show at zero current. The crossing slope is $-1/T$ exactly
(finite loop gain, not a nonlinearity), and the crossing offset is
$\SI{-1.1}{\nano\ampere}$ at the operational \SI{1}{\mega\ohm} electrode.

Table~\ref{tab:px-acc35} gives the operational accuracy at $R_f =
\SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ into the \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm} electrode: 0.41--0.61~LSB
worst-case error across the five process corners. Table~\ref{tab:px-hg1m-acc}
gives the operational accuracy at the maximum gain tap, $R_f = \SI{560}
{\kilo\ohm}$ into the \SI{1}{\mega\ohm} electrode operational at that gain:
0.253--0.376~LSB. These are the two gain taps with a matched
operational electrode simulated; the 140 and \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} rows measured
against the \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm} electrode (Table~\ref{tab:px-hg-demo}) are a
finite-loop-gain demonstration only and are not comparable accuracy figures --
see that table's caption.

At \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm} the error is range-dependent: 0.41--0.61~LSB over the
full $\pm\SI{33}{\micro\ampere}$ span, improving to 0.21--0.30~LSB over the
$\pm\SI{2.3}{\micro\ampere}$ subrange. The growth toward full scale is the
$1/T$ gain error of the transimpedance loop; the \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} figure is
already a full-scale measurement at its gain.
